newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends easier on recovery in stocks.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends easier on recovery in stocks.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures closed Friday's session easier as the Tokyo stock market recouped earlier losses to end firmer.
"Those who had gone long this morning quickly liquidated their positions to cut losses, and this resulted in a weaker close," said a dealer at a securities house.
The key contract was proved to be firmly capped at 99.23 before a major resistance point at 99.30, traders said.
"It looks more likely than before to many operators that Japanese interest rates will be raised, maybe by the summer," said a long-term credit bank dealer.
"Such a view may strengthen if U.S. jobs data due later in the day prompts anticipation of higher U.S. rates," he said.
The December was down 0.02 at 99.18 after moving between 99.18 and 99.23. A total of 45,705 contracts changed hands.

The Bank of Japan's (BOJ) operations on Friday morning showed it was taming banks' seasonal fund demand ahead of the fiscal year-end, and this resulted in a fall in short-term money rates, traders said.

The BOJ continued an accommodative credit stance for the sixth session in a row on Friday morning. The bank left the market in surplus by an estimated 80 billion yen by refraining from conducting a regular operation at 0020 GMT.
The bank later offered to buy a total of 600 billion yen in bills covering the fiscal year-end.
"It seems to me that the BOJ's operations were aimed at lowering the key overnight rate to what we see as a short-term bottom of 0.45 percent," a city bank dealer said.
The key overnight rate was mainly traded at 0.45 percent, sharply down from Thursday's weighted average of 0.48.
Another city bank dealer said the accommodative operations were also aimed at supporting the stock market.

"If it had been a neutral operation, stocks might have been sold because stock market sentiment has been hurt by news that executives at Nomura Securities Ltd conducted irregular deals with a client," the dealer said.

Trade was sluggish in the long end of the market. No three-, two- or one-month certificates of deposit (CD) were issued. Benchmark three-month CDs were offered at 0.54 percent, unchanged from Thursday's issued rate. -- Risa Maeda Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
